source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which is the correct sequence of the management functions?
questions.rationale: The management process: planning, organizing, staffing, leading (directing) and controlling, which is the last step.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Management functions (PDF p. 420)
questions.quote: The management functions are planning, organizing, staffing, leading or directing and controlling.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: The PHN compares the actual immunization coverage with the target and takes corrective action. This management function is:
questions.rationale: Controlling sets standards, compares actual performance with them, reports and takes corrective action.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Management functions (PDF p. 421)
questions.quote: Controlling is determining the actual performance compared with the desired output and taking the necessary corrective action/s

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Preparing an organizational chart showing lines of authority in the RHU is part of:
questions.rationale: Organizing designs the organization: structure, division of work, lines of authority and communication.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Management functions (PDF p. 421)
questions.quote: An organizational chart, shows the division of work, chain of command, type of work performed, grouping of work segments and levels of management

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Scheduling midwives and planning their staff development falls under which management function?
questions.rationale: Staffing covers selection, staff development, scheduling and assignments.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Management functions (PDF p. 421)
questions.quote: It includes selection of personnel, staff development, scheduling and giving assignments.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A supervisor who knows the midwives' jobs well enough to take their place in an emergency has strong:
questions.rationale: Technical skills are knowledge and skills related to the unit's services, processes and equipment.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Supervisor skills (PDF p. 421)
questions.quote: In a service delivery unit, a supervisor knows the job of his/her supervisees and can take their place in emergency situations.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A long-range plan containing the organization's vision, mission and broad objectives, often preceded by SWOT analysis, is a(n):
questions.rationale: Strategic plans are long-range; operational plans are short-range and deal with routine activities.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Planning (PDF p. 423)
questions.quote: A strategic plan is a long-range plan which contains an organizational vision and mission, guiding principles, broad strategic objectives

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A health center's plan to introduce a new queuing system for clients next month is part of its:
questions.rationale: An operational plan is a short-range plan addressing daily service delivery needs.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Planning (PDF p. 424)
questions.quote: An operational plan, on the other hand, is a short-range plan that generally deals with the routine activities of the organization.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A PHN receives conflicting orders from the chief nurse and the health center physician. Which principle of organization is being violated?
questions.rationale: Unity of command: each employee should receive orders from only one superior.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Principles of organization (PDF p. 425)
questions.quote: This principle means that an employee should be responsible to, and receive orders from, only one superior.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: The number of midwives reporting directly to a PHN refers to:
questions.rationale: Span of control is the number of subordinates reporting directly to a superior; it depends on competence, distance and work complexity.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Principles of organization (PDF p. 425)
questions.quote: Span of control means "the number of subordinates reporting directly to a superior"

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which factor would justify a smaller span of control for a PHN supervising midwives?
options: Midwives are widely scattered in far barangays
The work is simple and routine
questions.rationale: Span depends on subordinates' competence, geographic dispersion and complexity of work; dispersion favors fewer supervisees.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Principles of organization (PDF p. 425)
questions.quote: degree of geographical dispersion or how far the subordinates are from each other and how accessible they are to the supervisor

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A PHN is made EPI coordinator. To be effective, she must also be given:
questions.rationale: Authority should match responsibility; she is then accountable for program performance.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Principles of organization (PDF p. 425)
questions.quote: If a PHN, for example, is given responsibility as an EPI Coordinator she should also be granted corresponding authority

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under the devolved health system, who are the major decision-makers on local health budgets?
questions.rationale: Under devolution, the mayor and local council decide budgetary allocations that shape the local health system.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 The PHN as manager (PDF p. 423)
questions.quote: under a devolved set-up, the major decision-makers in health are the elected local officials

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Under the Philippine Nursing Act of 2002 (RA 9173), the minimum entry salary of nurses in government is:
questions.rationale: RA 9173 sets SG 15 as the minimum base pay for nurses in government service.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Staffing (PDF p. 426)
questions.quote: the Nursing Act of 2002 stipulates that the entry salary for nurses in government is SG 15.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: To convince local officials to hire more nurses, the PHN's best evidence is:
questions.rationale: Proper documentation (and time-and-motion studies) supports requests for increased staffing.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Staffing (PDF p. 426)
questions.quote: Nurses should properly and adequately document their activities so that their proposal for increased staffing will be considered seriously.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Leadership, in its essence, is best defined as:
questions.rationale: The essence of leadership is influencing others; PHNs lead by coaching, counseling, evaluating, delegating and rewarding.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 17 Leadership (PDF p. 426)
questions.quote: Its essence is influencing others. In an organizational context, it is "making people want to do something"
